accuracy.title: Why your official bracket may differ
items: Your official bracket uses income, assets and debt of your household (parents if single, spouse if married) collected by KOSAF through the Social Security Information System. The numbers you enter here may differ from those records.
Each item is taken from public records as of a set date, so recent changes in income or assets may not be reflected (see KOSAF's per-semester bracket guidelines).
Homes and land are valued at the official standard value (e.g., published price), not market price; cars at the Korea Insurance Development Institute value.

Only bank loans, student loans, lease deposits received and similar debts count; overdraft and credit-line loans, business loans and card loans do not. Unpaid card balances count only if 3+ months overdue and ₩500,000 or more (principal only).

Details such as the 50% deduction for a student's daily-wage income (larger than the ₩1.3M deduction only above ₩2.6M a month), overseas income and asset reporting, and sibling-deduction exclusions are simplified.
KOSAF has not finalized the 2027 thresholds, so they are estimated as the 2027 standard median income times each ratio. KOSAF plans to announce the final thresholds separately.
Amounts are based on the 2027 budget proposal and may change after the National Assembly passes the budget. Grade requirements and university eligibility restrictions also apply.

items.type1: National Scholarship Type I amounts — KOSAF

howTo.title: How to use
items: Enter income and assets for you and your parents if single, or you and your spouse if married. Do not include siblings' income or assets.
Enter income as a pre-tax monthly average and assets in ₩10,000 units. For homes, use the official standard value, not the market price.
The result shows your estimated bracket, the ratio to median income and how far you are from the next threshold. Add semester tuition to see what you pay.
If KOSAF already notified your bracket, choose 'I know my bracket'. Copying the link keeps all your inputs.

method.title: How the bracket is set
items: Monthly recognized income = assessed income + income-converted assets − sibling deduction
Income-converted assets = (assets − basic asset allowance ₩69M − debt) × monthly rate. The allowance and debt come off general assets first, then financial assets. Cars get neither.
Monthly rates: general assets and cars 4.17% ÷ 3, financial assets 6.26% ÷ 3. Every ₩10M counts as ₩139,000 a month (about ₩209,000 for financial assets).
₩1.3M is deducted from a student's wage or business income, and only 50% of daily-wage income counts. Single students in families with 3+ children get (children − 2) × ₩400,000 off.
Threshold = 4-person standard median income × bracket ratio (Ga 70%, Na 130%, Da 200%, Ra 300%), the same for every household size.

changes.title: What changes in 2027
items: From spring 2027, brackets 1–10 become five brackets Ga–Ma: former 1–3 → Ga, 4–6 → Na, 7–8 → Da, 9 → Ra, 10 → Ma.
Brackets that already received the same amount were merged, so Type I annual amounts are listed as Ga ₩6M, Na ₩4.4M, Da ₩3.6M and Ra ₩1M.
Multi-child 1st/2nd children: Ga ₩6.1M, Na ₩5.05M, Da ₩4.65M, Ra ₩1.35M a year; 3rd+ children: full tuition in Ga–Da and ₩2M in Ra.
The 2027 standard median income (4-person ₩6,929,885) is 6.7% higher than 2026, so thresholds are expected to rise. KOSAF will announce the final 2027 thresholds separately.

items.q: How is my National Scholarship bracket decided?
items.a: KOSAF collects the income, assets and debt of the student and household (parents if single, spouse if married) through the Social Security Information System, calculates monthly recognized income, and compares it with thresholds equal to the standard median income times each bracket ratio. Because the numbered brackets were often confused with statistical income deciles, they are renamed Ga–Ma from 2027.

items.q: Which old brackets do Ga, Na, Da, Ra and Ma correspond to?
items.a: Former 1–3 is Ga (up to 70% of median income), 4–6 is Na (up to 130%), 7–8 is Da (up to 200%), 9 is Ra (up to 300%) and 10 is Ma (over 300%). Basic livelihood recipients and near-poverty households remain a separate group.

items.q: Do thresholds change with household size?
items.a: No. KOSAF publishes one set of thresholds based on the 4-person standard median income times each ratio. Instead, single students in families with 3 or more children get (children − 2) × ₩400,000 off their recognized income, for example ₩800,000 a month with 4 children.

Per KOSAF's spring 2027 notice, the annual maximum is ₩6M for Ga (₩3M per semester), ₩4.4M for Na (₩2.2M), ₩3.6M for Da (₩1.8M) and ₩1M for Ra (₩0.5M); basic livelihood and near-poverty students get full tuition. Ma is not eligible. Awards never exceed tuition (required fees) and are based on the 2027 budget proposal, so they may change after the budget passes.

items.q: Who gets the multi-child scholarship, and how much?
items.a: Single students from families with 3 or more Korean-national children in bracket Ra or below. Students admitted from fall 2023 must have been 39 or younger at admission (40+ receive Type I instead). Annual amounts for 1st/2nd children are Ga ₩6.1M, Na ₩5.05M, Da ₩4.65M and Ra ₩1.35M; 3rd+ children get full tuition in basic livelihood/near-poverty and Ga–Da, and ₩2M in Ra. It takes priority over Type I and the two cannot be combined.

Yes. Round 1 for spring 2027 (Nov 24, 2026 09:00 – Jan 7, 2027 18:00 KST) is open to incoming, transfer, readmitted, returning and current students. Documents and family consent are due by Jan 14, 2027 18:00. Current students can, in principle, apply only in round 1; applying in round 2 is reviewed as relief, up to twice while enrolled.

Incoming, transfer and readmitted students have no grade requirement in their first semester. Current students need 12+ credits and a score of 80/100 or higher last semester; basic livelihood and near-poverty students need 70+, and students with disabilities are exempt. In bracket Ga, a score of 70–79 is allowed up to twice with a warning (C-grade warning system). Graduating or extra-semester students are exempt from the credit requirement.

items.q: What if my result differs from the bracket I was notified of?
items.a: The notified bracket is official because KOSAF uses public records. This calculator estimates from your inputs and the published method, so standard values, which debts count and record dates can cause differences. If your household income or assets changed a lot after the survey, check KOSAF's update request guide.
